title: Derive contract layout (FLAT, FACETED, COLLECTION) from the artifact name

facts.note: Contract schema, catalog and schema-test paths are matchable by glob (generic source pattern uses .json, concrete layouts .schema.json).
Schema files and planner artifacts (plans, wagons, WMBTs, acceptances, docs) that name artifacts or contract paths.
Task text mentions naming, placing, relocating or correcting a contract artifact/layout.
Needs a diff-level observer that detects new/renamed artifact names in planner artifacts and added/moved/renamed schema or schema-test files under contracts/.
Needs a detector mapping logical name to expected physical layout, comparing with the actual tree, and reporting source-ambiguous cases as unresolved.

values: planner states or chooses a contract layout
resource will hold several related schemas
facts.note: Whether the planner is choosing/stating a layout, and whether a resource will hold multiple schemas, needs semantic reading of the plan text.

fires: A plan or wagon declares a new artifact {domain}:{resource} and names where its contract schema will live.
A planner introduces a dot-faceted artifact name {domain}:{resource}.{category} in a produce/consume list.
A planner specifies a resource that will hold several related schema files under one artifact name.
A plan proposes contracts/{domain}/{resource}/{resource}.schema.json for a single-schema resource.
A task relocates, renames or corrects the layout of existing contract schemas or schema tests (e.g. flattening an over-nested resource, converting between FACETED and COLLECTION).
A doc or acceptance describes the expected contract path for an existing artifact name.
doesNotFire: Editing fields inside an existing schema without changing the artifact name, its file location or its test location.
Work that neither names, places, moves nor corrects any contract artifact or schema file.
Code-layer file placement outside contracts/ (governed by other layout conventions).

given: An artifact named {domain}:{resource}[.{category}] (colon = hierarchy, dot = facet; optional category for nested resources) is declared, or its contract schemas/tests are placed, moved or corrected
when: the planner chooses or states its contract layout under contracts/
then: Determine the layout in order: (1) dot facet → FACETED contracts/{domain}/{resource}/{category}.schema.json; (2) resource holding multiple schema files → COLLECTION contracts/{domain}/{resource}/*.schema.json; (3) otherwise → FLAT contracts/{domain}/{resource}.schema.json.
prefer: FLAT (single schema, single resource): tests contracts/{domain}/tests/{resource}_schema_test.*. Source examples: 'match:dilemma.current -> contracts/dilemma/current.schema.json # singular noun -> flat (NOT dilemma/current/current.schema.json)'; 'mechanic:decision.choice -> contracts/decision/choice.schema.json # single resource -> flat'; 'fragment:pool -> contracts/fragment/pool.schema.json'.

FACETED (category as dot facet): tests contracts/{domain}/{resource}/tests/{category}_schema_test.*. Source examples: 'ux:foundations.color -> contracts/commons/ux/foundations/color.schema.json # has dot facet -> nested; faceted, alternative to collection'; 'ux:primitives.icon'.

COLLECTION (one artifact, several related schemas in one directory): tests contracts/{domain}/{resource}/tests/*_schema_test.*; optional catalog.schema.json master index; each schema's metadata: collection: true, resource (same for all), member (identifies the schema). Source examples: 'ux:foundations -> contracts/commons/ux/foundations/*.schema.json # plural noun -> collection'; 'ux:primitives -> contracts/commons/ux/primitives/*.schema.json'.
Example comments cue noun number (plural → COLLECTION, singular → FLAT); the source gives no precedence over the order in then.

Unresolved source conflict: the dotted FLAT examples contradict 'dot → FACETED' with no stated criterion. Follow the order by default; if you depart, state the mapping in the plan and flag the ambiguity.

Source's generic physical pattern is contracts/{domain}/{resource}[/{category}].json, while the concrete layouts use .schema.json; this .json vs .schema.json discrepancy is unresolved—name the extension explicitly in the plan.
avoid: Over-nesting a single resource: 'fragment:pool -> contracts/fragment/pool/pool.schema.json' instead of contracts/fragment/pool.schema.json.
Contract paths not derivable from the logical name (layout chosen ad hoc).
why: A deterministic name→layout mapping lets the path be derived from the logical name, keeps simple resources flat and supports faceted and multi-schema resources without ambiguity; domain-based organization gives clear ownership and REST API mapping.
evidence: Every artifact name resolves to one layout per the determination order: FACETED contracts/{domain}/{resource}/{category}.schema.json, COLLECTION contracts/{domain}/{resource}/*.schema.json, or FLAT contracts/{domain}/{resource}.schema.json. Where a path matches only a source example that conflicts with the order (dotted name mapped FLAT, commons/ prefix, .json vs .schema.json), the outcome is 'unresolved conflict' for reviewer decision—neither auto-pass by example name nor auto-fail—and the plan must state the chosen mapping.
Schema tests sit in the tests/ directory matching the layout ({resource}_schema_test.*, {category}_schema_test.*, or *_schema_test.*).
COLLECTION members carry metadata {collection: true, resource: <shared>, member: <specific>}; optional catalog.schema.json acts as master index.
No single-schema resource is stored as contracts/{domain}/{resource}/{resource}.schema.json.
verifier_detail: Determination order: (1) a dot (.) in the name indicates FACETED, (2) multiple schema files indicate COLLECTION, (3) otherwise FLAT.

Logical pattern {domain}:{resource}[.{category}]; physical pattern contracts/{domain}/{resource}[/{category}].json (source writes .json in the generic pattern; concrete layouts use .schema.json — report the discrepancy as unresolved, do not silently normalise). Colon separator denotes hierarchy, dot separator denotes facet; optional category supports nested resources.

COLLECTION: artifact {domain}:{resource} → contracts/{domain}/{resource}/*.schema.json; tests contracts/{domain}/{resource}/tests/*_schema_test.*; optional catalog.schema.json master index; member metadata example: {"domain": "ux", "resource": "foundations", "collection": true, "member": "color"}; member e.g. 'color', 'spacing'; resource same for all e.g. 'foundations'.

Source examples (FLAT): 'match:dilemma.current -> contracts/dilemma/current.schema.json # singular noun -> flat (NOT dilemma/current/current.schema.json)'; 'fragment:pool -> contracts/fragment/pool.schema.json # single resource -> flat (NOT fragment/pool/pool.schema.json)'; 'mechanic:decision.choice -> contracts/decision/choice.schema.json # single resource -> flat'. The dotted names here map flat, in unresolved tension with dot→FACETED. Detector outcome for any dotted name mapped FLAT (including these example names) is 'unresolved conflict' requiring reviewer decision and an explicit mapping statement in the plan; matching an example name alone is not a compliance criterion.

Source examples (FACETED): 'ux:foundations.color -> contracts/commons/ux/foundations/color.schema.json # has dot facet -> nested'; also listed as 'faceted, alternative to collection'; 'ux:primitives.icon'. The commons/ prefix is literal example data with no stated routing rule; detector must not generalise it, and a path whose prefix is not derivable from {domain} is reported as 'unresolved conflict', not auto-accepted.

Source examples (COLLECTION): 'ux:foundations -> contracts/commons/ux/foundations/*.schema.json # plural noun -> collection (color, spacing, typography)'; 'ux:primitives -> contracts/commons/ux/primitives/*.schema.json # plural noun -> collection (icon, shape, mask)'. Heuristic from example comments: plural noun suggests COLLECTION, singular noun FLAT; no precedence over the determination order is stated.
Source counter-example: 'fragment:pool -> contracts/fragment/pool/pool.schema.json # over-nested; single resource must be flat'.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires and doesNotFire scenarios, including relocation/correction of existing layouts, plus an llm_judged fact for layout intent and multi-schema intent.
additions.justification: Required by the target schema; derived from the source statement (layout of any artifact), not new obligations.

additions.text: Follow the determination order by default; when departing from it for a dotted name, state the chosen mapping explicitly and flag the source ambiguity.
additions.justification: The source's dotted FLAT examples conflict with its dot→FACETED rule and give no criterion; defaulting to the stated rule and surfacing departures avoids inventing a resolution.

additions.text: States that the source gives no precedence between noun-number cues and the determination order.
additions.justification: Noting the absence is factual and avoids inventing a precedence.

additions.text: Name the extension explicitly in the plan given the .json vs .schema.json discrepancy.
additions.justification: The source's generic physical pattern (.json) conflicts with its concrete layouts (.schema.json); surfacing it to the planner without resolving it.

additions.text: 'Unresolved conflict' outcome for paths that only match source-conflicting examples (dotted FLAT, commons/ prefix, .json vs .schema.json).
additions.justification: Auditor required replacing name-specific compliance exemptions with an explicit unresolved-conflict outcome; preserves source ambiguity without accepting or rejecting by name.

additions.text: Dotted names mapped FLAT (including the source example names) produce 'unresolved conflict', not auto-pass.
additions.justification: Same as evidence[0]; avoids masking genuine mismatches for example names.

additions.text: commons/ prefix is literal example data, not a routing rule; non-derivable prefixes reported as unresolved conflict.
additions.justification: Removes unsupported generalisation while keeping the examples.

additions.text: Report the .json vs .schema.json discrepancy as unresolved; do not silently normalise.

additions.justification: Source examples (dotted FLAT, commons/ux paths), test paths, collection metadata, separator semantics and the two unresolved source conflicts must stay visible to the planner; losslessness wins over brevity.
